newsitem.title: USA: Main details of U.S. budget pact.
newsitem.headline: Main details of U.S. budget pact.

text.p: The Clinton administration and Congressional leadership announced late on Thursday they had reached agreement on the outline of a pact to balance the budget by 2002.
Many spending and tax details were still to be worked out by House and Senate committees but major provisions of the agreement were as follows.
TAX CUTS:
Net tax cuts of $85 billion through 2002 and not more than $250 billion through 2007. Including:
* Tax credit for children - $500 per child
* Capital gains tax cut (details to be determined)
* $35 billion in tax relief over five years for post-secondary education
* Expanded individual retirement accounts
In addition, House speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said they would seek to accommodate elements of Clinton's budget proposal including:
* Welfare-to-work tax credits
* District of Columbia tax incentives to spur growth
* Tax credits to clean up polluted industrial sites
(Tax offsets of $50 billion over five years include $30 billion by extending the life of the airline ticket tax)
SPENDING REDUCTIONS AND SAVINGS
Total spending reductions of $304 billion over five years. That amount includes:
* Slowing the growth of projected Medicare spending by $115 billion and Medicaid by $14 billion
* Defense reductions of $77 billion
* Other discretionary spending cuts of $61 billion
* $26 billion from sales of broadcast spectrum
* $14 billion in savings from declining interest rates
DEFICIT PATH AND ECONOMIC ASSUMPTIONS:
Assuming 2.1 percent annual economic growth the agreement expects the budget deficit to decline in the following manner (in billions of dollars):
deficit/surplus -67 -90 -90 -83 -53 1
